parole.significato: Musa textilis, a species of banana tree native to the Philippines grown for its textile, rope- and papermaking fibre.
parole.testo: From English abaca, from Spanish abacá (“abaca, Manilla hemp”), from Tagalog abaka (“abaca, Manilla hemp”), from Arabic أَبَق (ʔabaq, “abaca”), from Classical Syriac ܐܳܦܰܩܬܳܐ (ʾāpaqtā), ܐܰܦܩܰܥܬܳܐ (ʾap̄qaʿtā, “de-seeded cotton”) from ܦܩܰܥ (pqaʿ, “to split, to reave, to crack”).

Probably from English Eskimo, itself partly from Spanish esquimaos (“Eskimos”) and French Esquimaux (“Eskimos”), ultimately from an Algonquian language.
